basics.name: Mrunalini Ramnath
basics.summary: Machine learning engineer with 3+ years of production ML experience in finance and tech, currently pursuing a Master's in AI at Carnegie Mellon University. Proven track record of architecting high-throughput ML systems and real-time risk infrastructure, delivering a 4.8x throughput increase at Apple and a $15M+ annual benefit at American Express. Expertise in LLM systems, SFT, RAG and Agents.

education.institution: Birla Institute of Technology & Science, Pilani
education.studyType: B.E. Electronics & Communication Engineering; M.Sc. Physics

work.name: Apple
highlights: Engineered cache-aware intelligent request routing for Apple's internal enterprise GenAI platform serving 7M+ requests/day, delivering 4.8x throughput and 64% reduction in TTFT experimentally on production-like workloads.

Saved $350K annually on LLM infrastructure spend for the same workloads by extending KV-cache capacity beyond GPU VRAM, CPU cache offloading with llm-d, vLLM and LMCache across AWS and AliCloud K8s clusters.

work.name: American Express
highlights: Engineered feature optimization and modernisation for global credit card POS risk (20M+ transactions, 6M+ customers daily); drove 43% feature compression via clustering & variance-threshold pruning, achieving +6% Gini on XGBoost/AXGBoost.

Reduced compute/storage costs by 16% on 100M+ daily batch updates through intelligent feature selection; built feature performance dashboards and led global rollout strategy; Recognized with SVP Star of the Quarter 3x (top 0.01% of org).
Mentored multiple interns and new hires on onboarding and project progress.

work.name: American Express
highlights: Engineered feature enablement for global real-time payment risk system (2.5M+ payments, 1.5M+ customers daily); led IBM [mainframe-to-cloud migration](https://americanexpress.io/migrating-the-payments-network-twice/) of data across models, business strategy, and logs, leading to an annual $15M+ benefit.
Designed & built pre/post-migration production validation framework with automated feature quality checks and drift detection to validate XGBoost/AXGBoost model consistency across cutover.
Reduced feature dimensionality by 32% via tree-importance, correlation, and mutual-information filtering; achieved +4% Gini improvement and 12% compute/storage cost reduction on payment risk scoring.

work.name: American Express
highlights: Engineered production XGBoost credit-risk features impacting 80M+ cardholders; automated UAT & production integration validation for feature deployments saving 2500+ QA hours/quarter.
Remediated critical false-alerts in data drift monitoring system by 13%; improved alert precision by reducing feature noise.

work.name: Adobe
highlights: Audited 10+ K8s clusters using open-source tools; identified 15+ critical security gaps and improved vulnerability coverage by 26%.
Proposed remediation strategies that cut cluster monitoring overhead by 15% with no integration disruption.

work.name: Telangana E-Governance
highlights: Conceptualized and developed a website for automating municipality complaint registration and tracking.
Streamlined complaint handling by implementing a multi-level user hierarchy using Django and PostgreSQL.
Published dashboards for regular tracking using JS, HTML and CSS for the front-end of the website.

research.name: NL2SQL Agent
highlights: Developing a multi-agent RAG-based NL2SQL system for OracleSQL with execution-based verification.

research.name: Cross-Lingual Hallucination Detection in Multilingual LLMs
highlights: Established that correctness probes trained only on English hidden states of Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct can flag hallucinations zero-shot in South East Asian languages; best probe reached 0.704 AUC on English and 0.64 to 0.68 across target languages.

Implemented a full 28-layer sweep across six probe families and two extraction points, showing post-answer features and deeper layers transfer best and that the correctness signal is low-dimensional (random forests within 0.01 AUC of the MLP).

research.name: GraphAct: Graph-Structured Action Prediction for Web Agents
highlights: Architected a HTML-DOM graph attention network into a Qwen3-VL-8B backbone via a gated cross-attention adapter and LoRA.
Improved element accuracy from 12.7% to 49.5% and beat the strongest multimodal baseline by ~12 points with step accuracy reaching ~41%.

research.name: Outcome-Aware Fine-Tuning of Vision-Language Models for Web Agents
highlights: Ran a controlled study isolating outcome supervision for web agents: LoRA fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-8B on 6,445 matched Multimodal Mind2Web examples, nearly doubling Step Success Rate over the zero-shot baseline (31.99% to 62.32%).

Showed that adding structured page-transition labels to the training target gave no measurable gain over action-only SFT (task-level 95% CIs overlap), a null result that replicated across all three test splits.

Traced the regression to a terminal-action bias (predicting a child click over the parent hover) through dataset, schema, and failure-case analysis, supported by AXTree and chain-of-thought ablations.

research.name: PRISM: Probing Routed Information Flow via Structured Multimodal Bottlenecks
highlights: Designed and validated a hierarchical fusion variant outperforming the symmetric design by +2.7% (Acc2/F1); identified that asymmetric (AV/VA) fusion matches symmetric performance with fewer parameters, a key insight for production multimodal model design.
Researched fusion efficiency in multimodal models; discovered that scaling fusion capacity (4 to 12 tokens) on CMU-MOSEI/MOSI hurts performance (-6% correlation), revealing architectural waste.

research.name: ScleraNext: Lightweight CNN Segmentation for Real-Time Biometric Identification
highlights: Optimized a production iris/retinal segmentation pipeline: replaced a cascaded 2-stage segmentation CNN with a single compact model, reducing inference latency by 73% for edge deployment.
Benchmarked YOLO, U-Net, MobileNet, and DenseNet on accuracy/latency tradeoffs and selected an optimized U-Net-based model.

projects.name: ZulipGPT: LLM Integration for Chat Summarization in Open-Source Messaging
highlights: Shipped chat and inbox summarization into the Zulip open-source codebase with topic-drift detection and citation-backed prompts to reduce hallucination and injection risk.

Built a deterministic identity-masking pipeline using keyed pseudonym mapping before inference, providing a stronger privacy guarantee than post-hoc PII filtering since the model never sees real identities.
Cut summarization latency to under 15s via trigger-based invocation, rolling context windows, and message batching.

projects.name: Real-Time Movie Recommendation Platform
highlights: Trained an SVD collaborative filtering model on ~200K Kafka interactions; deployed a Flask API (<50ms latency) with Docker and automated retraining every 3 days. Designed a hybrid cold-start solution achieving 85%+ coverage on new users.

Built an end-to-end data pipeline (schema validation, drift detection, offline/online evaluation: NDCG@10 0.52, HR@10 0.68) with CI/CD testing (82% coverage). Set up a monitoring dashboard tracking >99% availability, model accuracy, costs, and data drift.
Designed A/B testing infrastructure, experimented, and found the cold-start strategy lifts NDCG@10 by 8%.

projects.name: SteelRAG: Hybrid Sparse-Dense Retrieval over a Crawled Local Knowledge Corpus
highlights: Built a 5,334-document corpus from 20+ sources via three targeted scraping rounds guided by gap analysis of ~117 unanswered question clusters; corpus expansion alone drove a +6.8% absolute gain in a combined F1 and LLM-judge score.
Implemented BM25 (bm25s), FAISS (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 384-dim), and Reciprocal Rank Fusion from scratch; hybrid RRF outperformed dense-only by +4.46% across F1, Recall, ROUGE-L, and LLM Judge.

Deployed Qwen2-7B-Instruct on a Modal A10G GPU; batch embedding cut index build from 3 hours to under 15 minutes, and reducing chunk size from 200 to 100 words improved F1 by +1.40% with no recall loss.
